acceptance: A recorded decision: accept the preflight backstop as sufficient for shell writes, or extend the hook.

If the hook is extended, it refuses a shell command that writes a tracked file in the primary clone, still permits read-only commands and make pr-arm-remote and pr-landing-remote, and has tests for both.
description: The pre-tool hook from PR #4143 checks the target path of file edit and write tools. It does not look at shell commands, so a redirect, sed -i, cp, git checkout or a script run with the primary clone as the working directory still changes tracked files there. The original defect (relative-path writes landing in the primary clone) came through file tools, so that path is covered; shell writes are caught only afterwards by the snapshot comparison in make agent-write-preflight. Decide whether detection after the fact is enough or whether the hook should also refuse shell commands whose working directory is the primary clone, allowing read-only commands and the remote close-out targets the repository rules permit there.
